nodes.label: Android and iOS Product Targets
nodes.rationale: Android and iOS are the only shipping targets; Windows remains a development harness.

nodes.label: Project Dependency Direction
nodes.rationale: Core owns integration interfaces so Core never depends on Integrations.

nodes.label: Source-Generated JSON Serialization
nodes.rationale: Android AOT and trimming can break reflection-based JSON that passes on Windows and in tests.

nodes.label: Raw SQLite Persistence
nodes.rationale: Hand-written repositories preserve explicit transaction, migration, pragma, and decimal behavior; no ORM is permitted without discussion.

nodes.label: Append-Only Migration Ledger
nodes.rationale: Shipped migrations are immutable; every schema change adds a numbered entry.

nodes.label: Decimal Money Stored as TEXT
nodes.rationale: SQLite REAL can lose cents, so money remains decimal end-to-end and aggregates run in C#.

nodes.label: Atomic Multi-Table Writes
nodes.rationale: Caller-owned transactions and no-partial-rows tests protect ingest, merge, plan write-back, and migrations.

nodes.label: AppStartup Loading Ready Error State Machine
nodes.norm_label: appstartup loading ready error state machine

nodes.label: Fail Loud Never Fake Policy
nodes.rationale: Integration and data failures must be actionable or visibly degraded; silent degradation and fabricated deal data are forbidden.

nodes.label: Real SQLite Test Strategy
nodes.rationale: Tests use migrated temp-file SQLite because pragmas, migrations, and decimal TEXT round trips are part of behavior.

nodes.label: Optimizer and Backfill Integrity Rules
nodes.rationale: Optimizer uses explicit savings gates without distance math; batch backfill skips receipts lacking confirmed dates because wrong dates poison price history.

nodes.label: Real Flyer Provider
nodes.rationale: Flyer-driven badges, labels, and swaps starve while FlippClient returns no deals, making provider wiring foundational.

nodes.label: Buy Stock-Up Wait Badges
nodes.rationale: One-glance shelf verdict reuses existing price-history signals instead of adding a new pricing engine.

nodes.label: Four-Week Stock-Up Quantity Hints
nodes.rationale: Purchase cadence suggests quantity while a four-week cap limits waste and budget spikes.

nodes.label: Zero-Effort Pantry Inference
nodes.rationale: Receipt recency and cadence provide a non-blocking hint without requiring pantry tracking.

nodes.label: Cheaper-Swap Suggestions
nodes.rationale: Suggestions depend on item category coverage, so live data quality must be verified before implementation.

nodes.label: Confirmed Receipt Date Rule
nodes.rationale: No guessed or statement-derived dates enter price history; illegible dates cause a skip with no write.

nodes.label: One Store per Chain
nodes.rationale: A thin corpus cannot support branch-level history; chain-level stores align with optimizer and flyer matching.

nodes.label: One-Photo Receipt Capture Policy
nodes.rationale: One file must equal one whole receipt because partial-photo splits create undetectable garbage partials.

nodes.label: Oldest-First Imports in Chunks of Ten
nodes.rationale: Small chunks limit blast radius and fatigue; oldest-first protects fading receipts and aids sanity checks.
nodes.norm_label: oldest-first imports in chunks of ten

nodes.label: Repeat-Item Cleanup Pass
nodes.rationale: Only repeat staples materially feed trends and alerts, so singleton cleanup is intentionally skipped.

nodes.label: Android Phone Backfill Data Home
nodes.rationale: With no sync and mobile-only product targets, backfill must run where the production database lives.

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled Local Notifications
nodes.rationale: A small ILocalNotifier avoids an unverified NuGet dependency while keeping notification failures isolated from receipt ingestion.

nodes.label: Receipt-Scoped Alert Scan
nodes.rationale: Global recent-receipt scans can misattribute backfilled alerts to the next single scan, so notification queries filter by receipt ID.

nodes.label: Android Smoke First and iOS Source-Gen Sweep
nodes.rationale: Android likely tolerates reflection JSON via JIT fallback; iOS full AOT warrants a complete source-generation and JsonDocument conversion before Mac work.
nodes.norm_label: android smoke first and ios source-gen sweep

nodes.label: Azure OCR Budget Guardrail
nodes.rationale: CAD 10 monthly budget alerts at 50 and 100 percent precede OCR smoke and backfill; runaway response is key revocation because budgets do not hard-stop usage.

nodes.label: Android r1 Bring-Up then r2 Notifications
nodes.rationale: A signed r1 and full smoke prove the deployment loop before notification work; r2 then proves in-place upgrade.
nodes.norm_label: android r1 bring-up then r2 notifications

nodes.label: Phase B iOS Gate
nodes.rationale: iOS starts only after Android exit and physical backfill, prioritizing data value before Mac cost.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Smoke Triage
nodes.rationale: Crashes, data loss, unusable features, and silent degradation block exit; awkward visual polish enters a backlog.

nodes.label: Post-Backfill Phase 3 Tuning
nodes.rationale: Real data drives fuzzy-match, optimizer-setting, and alert-noise decisions; code changes only if the fuzzy mis-map rate exceeds five percent.

nodes.label: Manual Emulator Restore Validation
nodes.rationale: With one user, adb-planted database validation proves backup viability; in-app restore waits for a second ring member or post-Phase-B.

nodes.label: Phone as Production Database
nodes.rationale: Phone owns real data from r1 onward; Windows remains fixture-only, with Drive backup after every backfill batch.
